model.rationale: The district's eleven-point Republican lean and Self's incumbency outweigh what is expected to be a better Democratic national environment, and fundraising points the same direction with Self well ahead. With no polls or ratings available, Polymarket's five percent price for Hunt is the main external check, and it matches the fundamentals-based read.
model.watch: Any late polling showing a single-digit race, or a sharp fundraising surge by Hunt, would be the clearest sign the district is drifting into play.
notes: No expert rater lists this race; treated as safe for the party holding the seat.

overview:
Texas's 3rd District, anchored in Collin County suburbs, leans Republican by about eleven points, and incumbent Keith Self is running for another term. No public polls or expert ratings track this race, so the outlook rests on district fundamentals, fundraising, and prediction markets. Self holds a clear money advantage, having raised more than $840,000 with outside-group support behind him, while Democrat Evan Hunt has raised about $447,000 and ends with modest cash on hand.

The national environment is expected to be more favorable to Democrats than in recent cycles, which narrows the expected gap but not enough to put the seat in play. Polymarket traders give Hunt roughly a five percent chance of an upset. The forecast expects Self to win by a comfortable double-digit margin, with wide uncertainty given the absence of polling.
